heads.en: NOTICE ON THE FOUR FOLLOWING LETTERS.

heads.la: EPISTOLA I. Adversus Arcadium, Eudoxiam, Arsacium ac Theophilum sententia profertur.
heads.en: EPISTLE I. Sentence is pronounced against Arcadius, Eudoxia, Arsacius and Theophilus.

heads.la: EPISTOLA [cn: d | In hac epistola repetitur, quod jam in antecedente scriptum erat. Quocirca opus esse suspicamur hominis otiosi, qui stylum exercere voluerit.] III. ARCADII IMPERATORIS AD INNOCENTIUM PAPAM. Se insontem esse eorum quae in legatos ipsius aut in Joannem admissa sunt, eorum auctores a se punitos. Adeoque relaxet sententiam, qua se cum conjuge a sacris mysteriis arcet.
heads.en: EPISTLE [nt: In this letter is repeated what had already been written in the preceding one. Wherefore we suspect it to be the work of an idle man who wished to exercise his style.] III. OF ARCADIUS THE EMPEROR TO POPE INNOCENT. That he is innocent of the things which were committed against his legates or against John; that their authors have been punished by him. And so let him relax the sentence by which he keeps him, with his consort, from the sacred mysteries.

heads.la: EPISTOLA [cn: a | Ex genuinis Innocentii epistolis 19, 21, 22 et 23, falsitas hujus, adeoque antecedentium, plane convincitur. In illis enim pacem is papa petentibus non temere, sed nonnisi praescriptis conditionibus, iisque completis, reddere probatur. Ex iis quidem conditionibus haec praecipua erat, ut Joannis nomen in sacras diptychas restitueretur. At nunc nec de Joannis nomine, nec de caeteris episcopis ipsi addictis, qui crudelissima exsilia velut Arcadii auctoritate patiebantur, nihil curat. Ita pontifex, cujus laudant majores nostri sapientiam non minus in restituenda, quam in auferenda personis augustis communione, imprudens fingitur.] IV.
heads.en: EPISTLE [nt: From the genuine letters of Innocent 19, 21, 22 and 23 the falsity of this one, and so of the preceding ones, is plainly proved. For in those this pope is shown to restore peace to those who asked for it, not rashly, but only on prescribed conditions, and those fulfilled. Of those conditions this indeed was the chief, that the name of John should be restored to the sacred diptychs. But now he cares nothing, neither about the name of John, nor about the other bishops attached to him, who were suffering most cruel exiles as if by the authority of Arcadius. So the pontiff, whose wisdom our forebears praise no less in restoring communion to august persons than in taking it away, is feigned to be imprudent.] IV.

headnotes.la: …ae Chrysostomi judicium oecumenicae synodo servasse. Quocirca is papa [n: (Innoc. epist. 5)] Theophilum, communionem cum ipso non secus atque cum Joanne habere se testatus, iteratis litteris hortatur,
headnotes.en: …e of Chrysostom to an ecumenical synod. Wherefore this pope [n: (Innoc. epist. 5)], having testified that he held communion with Theophilus no otherwise than with John, exhorts him by repeated letters
Likewise, writing to the people of Constantinople,

headnotes.la: Et ipsius rogatu Honorius imperator tertio ad Arcadium scripsit [n: (Epist. 9)], nullas intentans ei minas, sed tantum obsecrans,
headnotes.en: And at his request the emperor Honorius wrote a third time to Arcadius [n: (Epist. 9)], threatening him with no threats, but only beseeching

headnotes.la: …synodus, cum adversariis Joannis omnino rupit pacem atque communionem, sed eam intermisit tantum atque suspendit. Qua de re Palladius Vitae Chrysostomi scriptor sub finem dialogi pag. 214 ita loquitur
headnotes.en: …and communion with the adversaries of John, but only interrupted and suspended it. Of which matter Palladius, the writer of the Life of Chrysostom, speaks thus toward the end of the dialogue, page 214

headnotes.la: …rinos antistites recenseri etiam a Romanis praesulibus numquam desiit. Idem dicendum de caeteris ejus sociis, si excipiatur Arsacius, quem, Theodoreto teste [n: (lib. V, cap. 34)], Occidentis episcopi
headnotes.en: … bishops of Alexandria even by the Roman prelates. The same is to be said of his other associates, if Arsacius be excepted, whom, as Theodoret witnesses [n: (lib. V, cap. 34)], the bishops of the West

headnotes.la: …spensam tenere satis habuit, ad eam illi reddendam paratus, cum pactis conditionibus satisfecisset. Quocirca Maximiano episcopo eum amice roganti, ut pacificas ad Atticum litteras mitteret, rescripsit
headnotes.en: …on suspended, being ready to restore it to him when he had satisfied the agreed conditions. Wherefore, to the bishop Maximian, who amicably asked him to send letters of peace to Atticus, he wrote back
